mainTopic: Court summonses and נידוי, heirs returning stolen items, and money from customs collectors under דינא דמלכותא דינא
overview: The amud opens by limiting when a court may place someone in נידוי for ignoring a summons sent through a woman or a neighbor. If he was in town, passed by the courthouse, or did not come home that same day, the messenger may never have told him. רבא then teaches when a פתיחא is torn up, and רב חסדא rules that a court gives three dates, Monday, Thursday and Monday, before writing one. רב כהנא explains that a woman who is always in town and still does not come may get a פתיחא right away. רב יהודה and רב נחמן list times when no court date is set: ניסן, תשרי, ערב שבת and ערב יום טוב, and during Torah gatherings. Nowadays, because of tricksters, the court does summon people even during those gatherings. The גמרא then returns to the משנה: heirs must return even a well-known stolen animal, or a bed or table, for their father's honor. A new משנה forbids taking change or charity from the funds of customs and tax collectors. Each time the גמרא challenges a source with שמואל's rule דינא דמלכותא דינא, it answers that the collector had no fixed rate or appointed himself, and רב אשי adds that the collector was a non-Jew. That leads to a challenge, which continues on the next amud: רבי עקיבא himself teaches from a פסוק that גזל גוי is forbidden.

steps.title: No ostracism if the defendant is in the city
steps.stepSummary: An unofficial summons only counts if the defendant is out of town. If he is in the city, the messenger may have assumed the court's own שליח already told him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he is in the city, the court does not ostracize him. Maybe they never told him, because they thought: the court's messenger already found him and told him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is continuing an earlier rule that a summons sent through a woman or neighbor is valid. It adds a limit: this only applies when the defendant is not in town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the defendant is in town, the woman or neighbor may assume the court's official שליח will reach him. So they might not bother to tell him. Since he may never have heard about the summons, he cannot be punished for ignoring it.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps / one could say (raising a possibility)

phrases.english: But if he is in the city – no;
phrases.notes: 'No' means the court does not place him in נידוי for ignoring the summons. This continues the rule from just before this line.

phrases.english: for we say: perhaps they did not tell him,
phrases.notes: 'They' are the woman or neighbor who were asked to pass on the summons.

phrases.english: because they say: found him
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. The word in square brackets, 'found him', is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: the court's messenger, and told him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל אִיתֵיהּ בְּמָתָא – לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a limit on the earlier rule (from before this text) that a summons through a woman or neighbor is valid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the defendant is in the city, he is not ostracized for ignoring an unofficial summons. The messenger may have assumed the court's שליח told him.

steps.title: No ostracism if he passes by the courthouse
steps.stepSummary: A second limit: the rule applies only if the defendant does not pass the courthouse door. If he does, the messengers may assume the court told him directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only said this when he does not pass by the court's gate. But if he passes by the court's gate, the court does not ostracize him. The messengers say: the court found him and told him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second condition for punishing someone who ignores an unofficial summons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning is the same as before. If the defendant walks right past the courthouse, the messenger may think the court itself spoke to him. So the messenger may never deliver the summons, and the defendant cannot be blamed.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this when… (a formula that limits a rule)
At the gate (entrance) of the court

phrases.english: And we only said this
where he does not pass by the court's gate,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל חָלֵיף אַבָּבָא דְּבֵי דִינָא – לָא;
phrases.english: but if he passes by the court's gate – no;

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי: אַשְׁכְּחוּהּ בֵּי דִינָא, וְאָמְרִי לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: they say: the court found him, and told him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא חָלֵיף אַבָּבָא דְּבֵי דִּינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second limit using the same reasoning as step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the defendant passes the courthouse, he is not ostracized for ignoring an unofficial summons.

steps.title: No ostracism if he does not come home that same day
steps.stepSummary: A third limit: the defendant must come home on the same day the message was given. Otherwise the messenger may have simply forgotten.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only said this when he comes on that same day. But if he does not come that day, the court does not ostracize him. Say that they simply forgot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a third and final condition to the rule about unofficial summonses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reason is different from the first two. Here the messenger did not assume anyone else told him. They may simply have forgotten, because time passed before the defendant came home.
steps.whatToRemember: An unofficial summons, through a woman or neighbor, can lead to נידוי only if all three conditions hold. The defendant is out of town, he does not pass the courthouse, and he comes home that same day. Otherwise we suspect he never got the message.

phrases.english: And we only said this where he comes on that same day,
but if he does not come on that same day – no;
say that they simply forgot.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּאָתֵי בְּיוֹמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third limit and ends the list of conditions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the defendant does not come home that same day, he is not ostracized, since the messenger may have forgotten.

steps.title: רבא: when a document of ostracism is torn up
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches that a פתיחא is not torn up until the person actually does what he failed to do. That means coming to court, or obeying the ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: if a document of ostracism was written against someone because he did not come to court, we do not tear it up until he comes to court. If it was written because he did not obey the court, we do not tear it up until he obeys.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new topic: how a written document of נידוי gets cancelled. He gives two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases, רבא says a promise is not enough. The person must actually act, either by appearing in court or by carrying out the ruling. Only then is the document torn up.

keyTerms.meaning: A written document declaring a person in נידוי
We do not tear it up for him

phrases.english: Rava said:
One about whom a document of ostracism was written
because he did not come to court –

phrases.aramaic: עַד דְּאָתֵי לְדִינָא, לָא מְקָרְעִינַן לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: until he comes to court, we do not tear it up for him.
Because he did not obey the court's ruling –
until he obeys, we do not tear it up for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הַאי מַאן דִּכְתִיב עֲלֵיהּ פְּתִיחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from when נידוי is imposed to when its written document is cancelled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פתיחא stays until the person actually comes to court, or actually obeys the ruling, depending on why it was written.

steps.title: A promise to obey is enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבא's second case. Once the person says 'I will obey', the document is torn up right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is not so. Once he says 'I will obey', we tear it up for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא disagrees with the second half of רבא's statement, about someone who did not obey the ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For someone who refused to obey, the final ruling is that agreeing out loud to obey is enough to cancel the document. The first case, about not coming to court, is left standing: he still has to actually appear.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is not so (the גמרא rejects a statement)

steps.whatToRemember: Not coming to court: the פתיחא stays until he actually comes. Not obeying the ruling: the פתיחא is torn up as soon as he says 'I will obey'.
steps.confusionAlert: The words 'ולא היא' reject only רבא's second case, about obeying. His first case, about coming to court, still holds.

phrases.english: But it is not so;
phrases.notes: This is aimed only at רבא's second case, about not obeying the ruling.

phrases.english: once he has said: 'I will obey' –
we tear it up for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא, כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר: ״צָיֵיתְנָא״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the second half of רבא's statement in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only רבא's rule about someone who did not obey the ruling.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Actual obedience is not needed. A spoken commitment to obey is enough to cancel the פתיחא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For refusing to obey, saying 'I will obey' is enough to tear up the פתיחא.

steps.title: Three court dates before a פתיחא
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that the court sets three dates, Monday, Thursday, and the next Monday. Only on the day after the third missed date does it write a פתיחא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: We set a date for Monday, then Thursday, then Monday. That is a date, and another date after that date. On the next day we write the document.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives the schedule a court follows before it writes a פתיחא against someone who does not come to court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court does not punish after one missed summons. It gives three chances on the regular court days, and only after the third is missed does it write the פתיחא. This rule becomes the basis for the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: We set a date (for appearing in court)
Monday and Thursday, the regular days the courts sat

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
We set a date for Monday, then Thursday, then Monday,
a date, and another date after that date,
and on the next day we write [the פתיחא].
phrases.notes: The text just says 'we write.' It means the פתיחא, the document of נידוי from the earlier steps.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: קוֹבְעִים זְמַן שֵׁנִי וַחֲמִישִׁי וְשֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of the פתיחא from step 4 by setting out how many chances a person gets before it is written.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three court dates (Monday, Thursday, Monday) are given. The פתיחא is written on the day after the third missed date.

steps.title: רב אסי sees a פתיחא written after one missed date
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי visits רב כהנא. He sees a woman summoned in the evening who gets a פתיחא the next morning. He asks why רב כהנא did not follow רב חסדא's three dates.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי happened to visit the house of רב כהנא. He saw a certain woman who had been summoned to court in the evening, and in the morning a פתיחא was written against her. He said to him: Does the Master not hold of what רב חסדא said, that we set dates of Monday, Thursday, and Monday?
steps.whatsHappening: A story shows רב כהנא writing a פתיחא right away, and רב אסי challenges him with רב חסדא's rule of three dates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's rule says three chances must come first. Here the woman got only one chance, and the document was written the very next morning. רב אסי's question looks like an innocent question, but it is really a challenge against רב כהנא's practice.

keyTerms.meaning: A document of נידוי written against someone who will not come to court
Does the Master not hold of this?

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַסִּי אִיקְּלַע בֵּי רַב כָּהֲנָא.
phrases.english: Rav Asi happened to visit the house of Rav Kahana.
He saw a certain woman
whom he had summoned to court in the evening,
and in the morning he wrote a פתיחא against her.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר
phrases.english: He said to him: Does the Master not hold of
what Rav Chisda said:
'We set a date for Monday, Thursday, and Monday'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר לְהָא דְּאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רב חסדא's rule from step 6 to challenge a real case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's practice of writing a פתיחא after a single missed summons.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב חסדא requires three dates before a פתיחא. רב כהנא gave only one, so his practice seems to go against the rule.

steps.title: Three dates are for a man; a woman in town is a rebel
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers that the three dates apply to a man, who may be away for work. A woman is in town, so if she does not come, she is rebelling.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: These words apply to a man, who may be held up and not in the town. But a woman, since she is in the town and does not come, is rebellious.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא defends his practice by showing that רב חסדא's three dates were meant for a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra dates are given because a man may really be unable to come; he could be out of town working. A woman normally stays in town, so missing even one date shows she is refusing on purpose. That is why the פתיחא can be written right away. רב חסדא's rule still stands; it just does not cover this case.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply (only to a certain case)
Held up by circumstances beyond his control

steps.whatToRemember: The three dates exist to protect someone who may really be unable to come. If there is no such excuse, as with a woman who is in town, the court may write the פתיחא after one missed date.

phrases.english: He said to him: These words apply to a man,
who may be held up and not in the town;
but a woman, since she is in the town
and does not come, she is rebellious.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָנֵי מִילֵּי גַּבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אסי's challenge from step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the rule (אוקימתא to a man)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא's three dates apply to everyone, so writing a פתיחא after one date is wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: The three dates are only for someone who may truly be unable to come, like a man away for work. A woman in town who does not come is a rebel right away.

steps.title: No court dates during ניסן, תשרי, or the day before יום טוב and שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that the court does not set dates during the days of ניסן or תשרי, or on ערב יום טוב or ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: We do not give a date, not in the days of ניסן and not in the days of תשרי, not on the eve of יום טוב and not on the eve of שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching about court dates: times of year when the court does not call people to court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are busy times. ניסן and תשרי are full of preparations for the יום טוב, and people are busy on ערב שבת and ערב יום טוב. The court does not set a date then, since it is not fair to expect people to come.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
We do not give a date,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets, 'I give'. The word in square brackets, 'we give', is the corrected wording.

phrases.aramaic: לָא בְּיוֹמֵי נִיסָן וְלָא בְּיוֹמֵי תִּשְׁרֵי,
phrases.english: not in the days of Nisan and not in the days of Tishrei,

phrases.aramaic: לָא בְּמַעֲלֵי יוֹמָא טָבָא וְלָא בְּמַעֲלֵי שַׁבְּתָא.
phrases.english: not on the eve of a Festival and not on the eve of Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: לָא יָהֲבִינַן זִמְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new rule that stays on the same topic of setting court dates.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The court does not set dates during ניסן, during תשרי, on ערב יום טוב, or on ערב שבת.

steps.title: Setting a date for later: allowed in ניסן and תשרי, not on ערב שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה adds that during ניסן or תשרי the court may set a date for after the month. On ערב שבת it may not set a date for after שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But during ניסן we may set a date for after the days of ניסן, and during the days of תשרי for after תשרי. From ערב שבת we do not set a date for after ערב שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה continues and explains what the court may do during these busy times: may it set a date that falls later?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling someone to court during the busy time is forbidden, but in ניסן and תשרי it is fine to tell him about a date after the month. On ערב שבת, even telling him about a date after שבת is not allowed. The next step explains why ערב שבת is different.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two rules up. In ניסן and תשרי a date set for after the month is allowed. On ערב שבת a date set for after שבת is still not allowed.

phrases.english: But during Nisan, for after the days of Nisan,
and in the days of Tishrei for after Tishrei, we do set a date.

phrases.aramaic: מִמַּעֲלֵי שַׁבְּתָא לְבָתַר מַעֲלֵי שַׁבְּתָא – לָא קָבְעִינַן.
phrases.english: On the eve of Shabbat, for after the eve of Shabbat, we do not set a date.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל מִנִּיסָן לְבָתַר יוֹמֵי נִיסָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds details to רב יהודה's rule from step 9 about setting a date for a later time.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During ניסן and תשרי a date may be set for after the month. On ערב שבת a date may not be set for after שבת.

steps.title: Why ערב שבת is different: people are busy and may forget
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a date for after שבת cannot be set on ערב שבת. It answers that a person is busy with his שבת preparations.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? He is busy with his work for שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the ערב שבת rule and gives a short answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On ערב שבת a person's mind is on getting ready for שבת. If the court tells him about a date for after שבת, he may not pay attention and may forget it. Then it would be unfair to treat him as someone who refused to come.

keyTerms.meaning: His work for שבת, the preparations

steps.whatToRemember: The court sets dates in a way that is fair to the person called. It avoids busy times when he cannot come or may forget the summons.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
He is busy with his work for Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? בַּעֲבִידְתֵּיהּ דְּשַׁבְּתָא טְרִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for the ערב שבת rule in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a date for after שבת may not be set on ערב שבת, when a date for after the month may be set during ניסן and תשרי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: People are busy with שבת preparations and may forget the summons.

steps.title: No court dates for people gathered to learn Torah
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that the court does not set a date for people attending the כלה or the festival lectures while those gatherings are happening.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן says: We do not set a court date for people at the כלה during the כלה, nor for people at the festival lectures during the festival season.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן adds another time when the court does not summon people: while they are gathered to learn Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 9-11 listed busy times like ניסן, תשרי and ערב שבת. רב נחמן adds a different kind of exemption, people who came to learn Torah. They should not be pulled away to court during that time.

keyTerms.meaning: The big public Torah gatherings held in אלול and אדר
The festival season, with its public lectures before the יום טוב

phrases.english: Rav Nachman says:
We do not set a court date
not for participants in the kalla during the kalla,
phrases.notes: The כלה was the large gathering for Torah learning in the months of אלול and אדר.

phrases.english: nor for participants in the festival lectures during the festival season.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: לָא יָהֲבִינַן זִמְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another time-based exemption from court dates, alongside רב יהודה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No court date is set for people at the כלה or the festival lectures during those gatherings.

steps.title: רב נחמן sends away people who bring lawsuits during the kalla
steps.stepSummary: When people came to רב נחמן with claims during the כלה, he told them he had not gathered them for their own business.
steps.simpleTranslation: When people would come before רב נחמן with cases, he would say to them: Did I gather you here for your own needs?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells how רב נחמן actually behaved, which shows his rule from step 12 in action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gathering was called for Torah learning. Using it to chase down lawsuits would twist its purpose. So רב נחמן refused to hear such cases at that time.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲווֹ אָתוּ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן,
phrases.english: When people would come before Rav Nachman,
he would say to them:
Did I gather you for your own needs?!
phrases.notes: He means: I gathered you to learn Torah, not to settle your lawsuits.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֲווֹ אָתוּ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the reasoning behind רב נחמן's ruling through his own practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Torah gathering is for learning, so lawsuits are not heard then.

steps.title: Nowadays tricksters change the practice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that today, since some people come to the gatherings only to dodge their cases, the court is concerned and does summon them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But nowadays, when there are tricksters, we are concerned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the later practice: because of tricksters, the exemption from step 12 is no longer relied on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exemption was meant to protect real learners. Some people used it as a hiding place to avoid trial. So the court now worries about them and summons people even during these times.
steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן's rule was: no court dates during the כלה or festival lectures. Later, because tricksters used this to avoid trial, courts summoned people even then.

phrases.english: But nowadays, when there are tricksters,
we are concerned.
phrases.notes: So now the court does summon people even during these times, since some come only to dodge their case.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאִידָּנָא דְּאִיכָּא רַמָּאֵי חָיְישִׁינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רב נחמן's exemption in light of later conditions.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Because of tricksters, courts today do set dates even during the כלה and festival season.

steps.title: Heirs must return even a well-known stolen cow or donkey
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes our משנה about heirs paying for a stolen item that can serve as a guarantee. רבי explains that this includes a cow or donkey that everyone saw the father use, for the father's honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: If it was something that can serve as a guarantee, he must pay. רבי taught his son רבי שמעון: This does not only mean something that is really a guarantee, like land. Even a cow he plows with or a donkey he drives must be returned, because of the honor of their father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to our משנה about a thief who left stolen things to his children, and רבי explains how far the rule goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain words of the משנה suggest only land, which is a real guarantee for a loan. רבי widens the rule to well-known items like a work animal. People seeing the stolen animal would keep saying it was stolen, and this would shame the dead father.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that can serve as a guarantee for a loan (usually land)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the heirs' duty here comes from protecting the father's good name, so it reaches any item that people would notice.

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיָה דְבַר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ אַחְרָיוּת –
phrases.english: If it was something that can serve as a guarantee,
phrases.notes: This is a quote from our משנה about the children of a thief.

phrases.english: he is obligated to pay.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנֵי לֵיהּ רַבִּי לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרֵיהּ:
phrases.english: Rebbi taught it to Rabbi Shimon his son:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ אַחְרָיוּת מַמָּשׁ,
phrases.english: Not only something that actually serves as a guarantee,
but even a cow that he plows with,
a donkey that he drives from behind,
they are obligated to return,
because of the honor of their father.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנֵי לֵיהּ רַבִּי לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of court dates and returns to explain a line in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heirs must return even a well-known stolen work animal, because of their father's honor.

steps.title: What about a stolen bed or table?
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא asks רב whether heirs must also return a stolen bed or table, which are used at home and less public.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא asked רב: A bed that he reclines on, or a table that he eats on, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא asks whether רבי's rule from step 15 also covers household items that are used more privately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cow or donkey is seen by everyone in the fields and streets. A bed or table is used inside the house, so fewer people would notice. The question is whether the father's honor is still at stake.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana asked of Rav:
a bed that he reclines on,
a table that he eats on,
what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא מֵרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the limits of רבי's rule with less public items.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Must heirs return a stolen bed or table, which are used privately, for the father's honor?

steps.title: רב: a wise man can work it out
steps.stepSummary: רב answers with a פסוק, hinting that רב כהנא can learn the answer himself from the cow and donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: "Give to a wise man, and he will become even wiser."
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question with a פסוק, meaning the answer follows from what was already taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב does not give a new rule. He hints that the reasoning about the cow and donkey also applies to a bed and table. So the heirs must return them too.

keyTerms.meaning: Give to a wise man and he will become wiser (משלי 9:9)

steps.whatToRemember: Heirs must return stolen items people would recognize: land, a cow, a donkey, and also a bed or table, for the honor of their father.

phrases.english: He said to him:
"Give to a wise man, and he will become even wiser."
phrases.notes: משלי 9:9. He means: you can figure this out yourself from the cow and donkey.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: תֵּן לְחָכָם וְיֶחְכַּם עוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב כהנא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes: just as a cow and donkey must be returned, so must a bed and table.

steps.title: משנה: Do not take money from tax collectors' funds
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that one may not make change from the trunk of customs collectors or the purse of tax collectors, nor take charity from them. But one may take money from the collector's house or from the market.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may not make change from the box of customs collectors, nor from the purse of tax collectors, and one may not take charity from them. But one may take from his house or from the market.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, teaching about money held by customs and tax collectors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The money in the collection box or purse is assumed to be taken unfairly, so one should not take it even as change or charity. Money from the collector's home or that he has with him in the market is not from the collection, so it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Exchange large coins for small ones (make change)

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is only money from the collection box or purse. Money from the collector's own home or the market is allowed.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One may not make change from the box of customs collectors,
nor from the purse of tax collectors,
and one may not take charity from them.
But one may take from his house
or from the market.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין פּוֹרְטִין לֹא מִתֵּיבַת הַמּוֹכְסִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not take change or charity from collectors' boxes or purses. Money from their house or the market is permitted.

steps.title: You may pay with a coin and take back change
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds that although one may not make change from the customs trunk, one may give the collector a דינר and accept the change back.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: But he may give him a דינר, and the collector may give him back the rest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that softens the משנה's rule. Paying a customs collector with a larger coin and getting change back is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbade making change from the collector's trunk, because the money in it may be stolen. The ברייתא says that when you owe the collector money, you may hand him a דינר and take back what is left over. This is not a normal money exchange. It is just part of paying what you owe.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught:
But one may give him a dinar,
phrases.notes: "Him" is the customs collector, and the dinar pays a fee that is smaller than a dinar.

phrases.english: and he gives him back the rest.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: אֲבָל נוֹתֵן לוֹ דִּינָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to the משנה from Step 18
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may pay the collector with a large coin and receive change.

steps.title: Isn't the law of the kingdom binding?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: if דינא דמלכותא דינא, then customs money is collected legally, so why treat it as stolen?
steps.simpleTranslation: Regarding customs collectors: But didn't שמואל say that the law of the kingdom is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's rule about customs collectors by quoting שמואל's well-known principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל teaches that the government's laws are binding. If so, a customs collector is collecting money by law, so his money should not be treated as stolen. That seems to clash with the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The law of the kingdom is binding law

phrases.english: "And customs collectors."
But didn't Shmuel say:
The law of the kingdom is the law!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: דִּינָא דְמַלְכוּתָא דִּינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's rule about customs collectors
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule treating customs money as stolen
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If government law is binding, customs are collected legally and are not theft.

steps.title: A collector with no set limit
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בר כהנא, quoting שמואל, answers that the משנה is talking about a collector who has no fixed rate.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בר כהנא said in the name of שמואל: The משנה means a customs collector who has no fixed limit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The משנה is talking about a collector who takes as much as he wants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דינא דמלכותא only protects what the government actually set. A collector with no fixed amount takes more than the law allows, and that extra money is theft. So both rules stand.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who reports שמואל's answer

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that דינא דמלכותא is not a blank check. It only covers taxes that the government itself has set.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina bar Kahana said
that Shmuel said:
It is about a customs collector who has no limit.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמוֹכֵס שֶׁאֵין לוֹ קִצְבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 20
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה forbids the money of every customs collector, which clashes with דינא דמלכותא.
steps.terutzMaskana: It only forbids the money of a collector who takes without a fixed limit.

steps.title: A collector who appointed himself
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ינאי gives another answer: the משנה is talking about a collector who was never appointed by the government.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי said: The משנה means a customs collector who set himself up on his own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the same challenge. This collector has no government authority at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A self-appointed collector is not acting for the kingdom, so דינא דמלכותא does not apply to him at all. Whatever he takes is simply stolen.

keyTerms.meaning: Who stands on his own, meaning self-appointed

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai say:
It is about a customs collector who stands on his own.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי אָמְרִי: בְּמוֹכֵס הָעוֹמֵד מֵאֵלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the קשיא of Step 20
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The collector is acting for the government.
steps.terutzMaskana: He appointed himself, so דינא דמלכותא does not cover him.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's ban fits with דינא דמלכותא because it is only about a collector with no fixed limit, or one who appointed himself.

steps.title: Some attach this to the משנה about wearing כלאים
steps.stepSummary: Some teach this discussion on a different משנה, which says a person may not wear כלאים, even on top of ten garments, in order to avoid customs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach this on the following משנה: A person may not wear כלאים, even on top of ten garments, in order to sneak it past the customs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of where this discussion belongs. It is setting up a new context for the same question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Customs collectors did not charge for clothing a person was wearing. People would therefore wear their goods to avoid paying. The משנה forbids doing this with a כלאים garment, even when it is worn only as a top layer over many other garments.

keyTerms.meaning: Some teach it on this other source
Forbidden mixture of wool and linen

phrases.english: There are those who teach it on this:
A person may not wear diverse kinds
even on top of ten garments,
to sneak past the customs with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לַהּ אַהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves the answers of Steps 21-22 to a different משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not wear כלאים to avoid customs.

steps.title: This משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the כלאים משנה does not follow the view of רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is not like רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes an observation about who the author of the כלאים משנה could be. It sets up a proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's wording takes for granted that sneaking past customs is something a person would want to do but must not do with כלאים. The גמרא says that this does not fit רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: The mishna is not in accordance with Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies whose view the משנה from Step 23 follows
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כלאים משנה is not like רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: The ברייתא: may one avoid customs?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the dispute. The first view forbids avoiding customs, while רבי שמעון, quoting רבי עקיבא, permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: It is forbidden to sneak past the customs. רבי שמעון says in the name of רבי עקיבא: It is permitted to sneak past the customs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves its claim from a ברייתא where רבי עקיבא allows a person to avoid customs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא allows wearing כלאים to avoid customs. The כלאים משנה forbids it, so the משנה must follow the first, anonymous view. The גמרא will explain this dispute in step 26 and then challenge the customs part with דינא דמלכותא in step 27.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
A תנא, student of רבי עקיבא

steps.confusionAlert: The argument is about the כלאים. רבי עקיבא allows wearing the כלאים garment in this way, since he does not intend to benefit from wearing it (step 26). The question about avoiding the tax itself comes up in step 27.

phrases.english: As it was taught:
It is forbidden to sneak past the customs.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says in the name of Rabbi Akiva:
It is permitted to sneak past the customs.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אָסוּר לְהַבְרִיחַ אֶת הַמֶּכֶס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the claim of Step 24
steps.raayaObject: That the כלאים משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי עקיבא permits avoiding customs

steps.title: Explaining the כלאים dispute as a debate about unintended acts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the dispute about wearing כלאים is about דבר שאין מתכוין: one view permits an unintended act, the other forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, on the issue of כלאים, we understand what they argue about. One holds that an unintended act is permitted, and the other holds that an unintended act is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the כלאים side of the ברייתא from Step 25. It is setting up a question it will ask in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person wears the כלאים only to fool the customs collector. He does not mean to enjoy wearing it. רבי עקיבא allows this because the forbidden part is not what he intends, while the first view forbids it anyway. The word בשלמא ('granted') signals that the real difficulty is coming next.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / this part is understandable (sets up a difficulty with another part)
Forbidden mixture, here wool and linen worn together (שעטנז)
An act whose forbidden result the person does not intend

phrases.english: Granted, regarding the issue of diverse kinds,
this is what they disagree about:
that one Sage holds:
phrases.notes: This is רבי עקיבא, who permitted it in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: an unintended act is permitted,
and the other Sage holds:
an unintended act is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְעִנְיַן כִּלְאַיִם, בְּהָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the two views in the ברייתא quoted in Step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כלאים dispute is about whether an unintended forbidden act is allowed.

steps.title: How can evading customs be allowed if the king's law is binding?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: even if the כלאים part is fine, how can avoiding customs be allowed when שמואל says דינא דמלכותא דינא?
steps.simpleTranslation: But is it even allowed to sneak past the customs? Didn't שמואל say: the law of the kingdom is the law!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the other half of the case. Whatever the rule about כלאים, avoiding customs itself seems forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither view in the ברייתא objected to dodging the tax. They only argued about the כלאים. But שמואל teaches that government law is binding, so cheating a legal customs official should be forbidden no matter what.

keyTerms.meaning: The law of the government is binding law

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about כלאים at all. It is about whether dodging the tax is allowed, which both views in the ברייתא seemed to assume.
steps.whyThisMatters: דינא דמלכותא דינא is a major rule in practical הלכה about taxes and civil law.

phrases.english: But to evade the customs with it,
is that permitted?
But didn't שמואל say:
The law of the kingdom is the law!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְהַבְרִיחַ בּוֹ אֶת הַמֶּכֶס – מִי שְׁרֵי? וְהָאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After granting the כלאים logic in Step 26, the גמרא challenges the customs-evasion part.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's assumption that evading customs is acceptable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל rules that government law is binding, so evading a lawful tax should be forbidden.

steps.title: Answer: the collector has no fixed rate
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בר כהנא quoting שמואל answers that the case is a collector who has no fixed limit on what he takes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בר כהנא said in the name of שמואל: we are talking about a customs collector who has no set limit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It does this by narrowing the case to a collector who charges whatever he wants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דינא דמלכותא דינא only covers a real, orderly law. A collector who has no fixed rate is acting on his own whim, not enforcing the king's law, so avoiding him is allowed. This is the same answer given in Step 21, now applied to the כלאים ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina bar Kahana said
that Shmuel said:
It is about a customs collector who has no set limit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר כָּהֲנָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: בְּמוֹכֵס שֶׁאֵין לוֹ קִצְבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 27.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any customs collector is enforcing binding government law.
steps.terutzMaskana: A collector with no fixed rate is not enforcing real law, so evading him is allowed.

steps.title: Another answer: the collector was never appointed
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ינאי answers that the case is a self-appointed collector.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי said: we are talking about a customs collector who set himself up on his own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer to the same challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the problem is not the amount he charges but his authority. A collector the government never appointed has no 'law of the kingdom' behind him, so avoiding him is permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: Avoiding customs is only allowed when the collector is not truly enforcing government law: either he has no fixed rate, or he was never appointed.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai say:
It is about a customs collector who stands on his own.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי אָמְרִי: בְּמוֹכֵס הָעוֹמֵד מֵאֵלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative answer to the challenge of Step 27, alongside Step 28.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The collector is a legitimate government official.
steps.terutzMaskana: A self-appointed collector has no legal authority, so evading him is allowed.

steps.title: Another version: the משנה about vowing before customs collectors
steps.stepSummary: Some place the whole discussion on a משנה in נדרים that allows a false vow before murderers, robbers, and customs collectors to protect one's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach this discussion on a different משנה: One may make a vow to murderers, robbers, and customs collectors, saying the item is תרומה or belongs to the king's house, even though it is not תרומה and does not belong to the king.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a different tradition about where this discussion belongs. It quotes a משנה from נדרים to set up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows a person to back up a false claim with a vow, so that thieves or collectors won't take his property. Murderers and robbers are clearly not lawful, but listing customs collectors next to them seems strange. The next step raises exactly that problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Some teach it on this (another version places the discussion here)
Produce given to the כהן, which others may not eat

phrases.english: And some teach it on this:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in נדרים 27b.

phrases.english: One may vow to murderers,
and to robbers and to customs collectors,
that it is תרומה,
that it belongs to the king's house;

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָהּ שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה,
phrases.english: even though it is not תרומה,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָהּ שֶׁל מֶלֶךְ:
phrases.english: even though it does not belong to the king.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי אַהָא: נוֹדְרִין לֶהָרָגִין וְלֶחָרָמִין וְלַמּוֹכְסִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Like Step 23, gives another tradition placing the same discussion on a different משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may make a false vow before murderers, robbers, and customs collectors to protect property.

steps.title: How can one deceive customs collectors if the king's law is binding?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the משנה can permit a false vow before customs collectors, given דינא דמלכותא דינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And to customs collectors too?! But didn't שמואל say: the law of the kingdom is the law!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה from נדרים with the same rule of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Murderers and robbers have no right to your property, but a customs collector enforces government law. So tricking him should be forbidden. This is the same attack as Step 27, now aimed at the נדרים משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say? (opens a challenge from an accepted statement)

phrases.english: And to customs collectors?!
But didn't Shmuel say:
The law of the kingdom is the law!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלַמּוֹכְסִין?! וְהָאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: דִּינָא דְמַלְכוּתָא דִּינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה quoted in Step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's permission to make a false vow before customs collectors
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Customs collectors enforce binding government law, so deceiving them should be forbidden.

steps.title: Answer: the collector has no fixed rate
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בר כהנא quoting שמואל answers that the משנה is about a collector with no fixed limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בר כהנא said in the name of שמואל: the משנה is about a customs collector who has no set limit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge on the נדרים משנה with the same answer it used before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A collector who takes whatever he wants is not carrying out real government law. So the משנה may treat him like the robbers listed with him.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina bar Kahana said
that Shmuel said:
It is about a customs collector who has no set limit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר כָּהֲנָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: בְּמוֹכֵס שֶׁאֵין לוֹ קִצְבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 31.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's customs collector is a lawful official.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a collector with no fixed rate, who is not enforcing real law.

steps.title: Another answer: the collector was never appointed
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ינאי answers that the משנה is about a self-appointed collector.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי said: the משנה is about a customs collector who set himself up on his own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second answer to the challenge on the נדרים משנה. A third answer, from רב אשי, comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A self-appointed collector has no government authority behind him, so a vow to protect one's goods from him is allowed. In both versions the same two answers solve the problem with שמואל's rule.
steps.whatToRemember: Whichever משנה this discussion is placed on, the answer is the same: דינא דמלכותא דינא protects only a lawful collector. One with no fixed rate, or one who appointed himself, may be avoided.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai say:
It is about a customs collector who stands on his own.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי אָמְרִי: בְּמוֹכֵס הָעוֹמֵד מֵאֵלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative answer to Step 31, alongside Step 32.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The collector is a legitimate appointee.
steps.terutzMaskana: A self-appointed collector has no legal authority, so the vow is allowed.

steps.title: רב אשי: The משנה Is About a Non-Jewish Collector
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers the earlier question by saying the משנה permits a false vow only before a non-Jewish customs collector.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The משנה is talking about a non-Jewish customs collector.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a third answer to the question of how the משנה can permit a false vow before a customs collector. He says the collector in the משנה is not Jewish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answers said the collector had no fixed limit (שמואל) or appointed himself (the school of רבי ינאי). רב אשי takes a different route. He does not change what the collector is doing; he changes who the collector is. He will now bring a ברייתא to show that this kind of dealing is allowed with a non-Jew.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
[The משנה is speaking] about a non-Jewish customs collector.
phrases.notes: He is answering the question from before: how can the משנה in נדרים allow a false vow before a customs collector?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: בְּמוֹכֵס גּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the קשיא of step 31, alongside the answers of steps 32 and 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the collector is a non-Jew.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seems to permit misleading any lawful collector, which would clash with דינא דמלכותא דינא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a non-Jewish collector, and a ברייתא will be brought to support this.

steps.title: The ברייתא About a Court Case Between a Jew and a Non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a dispute between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא about whether the court may work its way around to a win for the Jew when the law does not favor him.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: When a Jew and a non-Jew come to court, if you can rule for the Jew under Jewish law, rule for him and tell the non-Jew, 'This is our law.' If you can rule for the Jew under non-Jewish law, rule for him and tell the non-Jew, 'This is your law.' If neither works, the court comes at the case in a roundabout way. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל. רבי עקיבא says: the court does not come at the case in a roundabout way, because of קידוש השם.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings a ברייתא to support his answer. It describes how a court handles a case between a Jew and a non-Jew, and records a disagreement between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree the court may pick whichever legal system favors the Jew. They argue only about the case where neither system helps. רבי ישמעאל allows a roundabout approach. רבי עקיבא forbids it, and the reason he gives is קידוש השם.

keyTerms.meaning: Sanctifying God's name, showing honor to Him in how we act

steps.confusionAlert: Read רבי עקיבא's words carefully. He does not say the roundabout approach is wrong in itself. He says it is not done 'because of קידוש השם.' The next step depends on exactly this wording.

phrases.english: As it is taught: A Jew and a non-Jew who came to judgment,

phrases.aramaic: אִם אַתָּה יָכוֹל לְזַכּוֹתוֹ בְּדִינֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל –
phrases.english: if you can rule in his favor under Jewish law,
rule in his favor, and say to him: 'This is our law.'
phrases.notes: 'Say to him' means say it to the non-Jew.

phrases.english: [If you can do so] under non-Jewish law, rule in his favor
and say to him: 'This is your law.'
And if not, they come at him in a roundabout way;
these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.
Rabbi Akiva says:
They do not come at him in a roundabout way,
because of the sanctification of God's name.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹי שֶׁבָּאוּ לַדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source that backs רב אשי's answer.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's claim that the משנה can permit misleading a non-Jewish collector.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the dispute between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא about court cases between a Jew and a non-Jew.

steps.title: Even רבי עקיבא Agrees When No קידוש השם Is Involved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads רבי עקיבא's reason closely: he holds back only because of קידוש השם, so where that concern is missing, even he allows the roundabout approach.
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for רבי עקיבא: his reason is that קידוש השם is involved. So where קידוש השם is not involved, the court does come at the case in a roundabout way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the exact wording of רבי עקיבא's reason. This shows the ברייתא supports רב אשי according to both opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל clearly allows the roundabout approach. רבי עקיבא's only objection is קידוש השם, so where that concern does not apply, he would allow it too. That makes the ברייתא a support for רב אשי according to everyone.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva:
the reason is that there is [a concern of] sanctifying God's name,
but where there is no [concern of] sanctifying God's name, they do come [at him in a roundabout way];

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא טַעְמָא דְּאִיכָּא קִידּוּשׁ הַשֵּׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carefully reads רבי עקיבא's reason from the ברייתא in step 35.
steps.raayaObject: That roundabout dealing with a non-Jew is allowed according to both opinions when קידוש השם is not involved.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording of רבי עקיבא's reason, 'מפני קידוש השם'.

steps.title: Challenge: Is Robbing a Non-Jew Really Allowed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the conclusion just drawn by quoting a ברייתא in which רבי עקיבא himself derives from a פסוק that גזל גוי is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But is robbing a non-Jew permitted? Isn't it taught: רבי שמעון said, רבי עקיבא expounded this when he came from זפירין: From where do we know that robbing a non-Jew is forbidden? The פסוק says: 'After he is sold, he may be redeemed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the idea that one may take from a non-Jew in a roundabout way. It starts quoting a ברייתא in which רבי עקיבא teaches that גזל גוי is forbidden, citing a פסוק. The ברייתא continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous step made it sound as if even רבי עקיבא allows taking from a non-Jew when קידוש השם is not involved. Now a ברייתא has רבי עקיבא himself deriving from a פסוק that robbing a non-Jew is forbidden. The two seem to contradict each other, and the explanation of the פסוק comes in the next part of the ברייתא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge sets up the larger question of how to fit together the ban on גזל גוי with the rulings that seemed to allow taking from a non-Jew.

phrases.english: But is robbing a non-Jew permitted?
But isn't it taught: Rabbi Shimon said,
this matter Rabbi Akiva expounded
when he came from Zephirin:
From where [do we know] that robbing a non-Jew is forbidden?
The verse says:
'After he is sold, he may be redeemed' –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:48. The ברייתא keeps going after this line.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְגֶזֶל גּוֹי מִי שְׁרֵי? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the inference of step 36 that roundabout taking from a non-Jew is allowed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that even רבי עקיבא would allow coming at a non-Jew in a roundabout way when קידוש השם is not involved.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא himself teaches, from a פסוק, that robbing a non-Jew is forbidden. So how can he allow taking from a non-Jew in any case?
